translations.text: All alone in my little hut, without a single person with me: such a little pilgrimage would be dear to me before going to meet death.
A remote, hidden little hut for the forgiveness of every wrong; an upright, spotless conscience directed towards holy heaven.
Making the body holy through good habits; trampling manfully on it; with weak, tearful eyes, for the forgiveness of my desires.
Desires feeble and withered; renouncing this wretched world; pure, lively thoughts: let that be the entreaty to God.
Lamentations with fervour towards cloudy heaven; sincere and truthful confessions; swift showers of tears.
A cold and fearful bed, like the lying down of a doomed man; a short, anxious sleep; cries to God, frequent and early.
My food, my situation: dear would be the confinement; my meal would not make me sinful, without doubt.
Dry bread weighed out (well may we bow our faces); water from the bright-coloured hillside: that would be the drink you would take.
A bitter, meagre meal; the mind diligent on a book; a hand set against strife and against visiting; a conscience serene and untroubled.
Dear, nevertheless, would be pure, holy blemishes: dry, thin cheeks, a leathery, lean skin. Stanza 11 is relegated to the notes by the editor; here it is printed from the notes, page 179.
Stepping along the paths of the Gospel; singing psalms at every hour; an end to talk and to long stories; constant bending of the knee.
May Christ, the Son of God, visit me, my Creator, my King; may my mind turn to him in the kingdom where he is.

May this be the place that encloses me, among the enclosures of churches: a lovely little place with holy graves, and I alone there. Stanza 14 is relegated to the notes by the editor; here it is printed from the notes, page 180.

All alone in my little oratory, all alone like this; alone I came into the world; alone I shall go from it. Stanza 15 is relegated to the notes by the editor; here it is printed from the notes, page 180.
If, alone, I have taken anything from the pride of this world, hear my lament as I weep, all alone, O God.
